prize_parts.citation: for the development of general ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize to Buchwald and Hartwig. The round-1 exchange tested it on novelty, priority and distinctness from 2010, and I find it holds. It is the only shortlisted candidate that no member disputes on maturity, and every member who commented on it agrees on the pairing. The chemical argument for distinctness is concrete. The 2010 prize concerned C-C bond formation with organometallic partners. C-N coupling had a different bottleneck, namely amine binding and reductive elimination from an amido-palladium complex, and it needed new ligand classes (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkylphosphines) to work at all. The Migita/Kosugi stannylamine reaction used stoichiometric tin reagents and had narrow scope. What made the reaction a tool was the catalytic system with free amines and a base, and that is the general method Buchwald and Hartwig delivered independently. The citation should say general, ligand-controlled and catalytic, so the precursor is acknowledged by what the words exclude. Two names keep the attribution clean and leave the third seat unused, which I regard as a virtue and not a gap.
statement.case_against: The overlap with 2010 remains a legitimate objection for any member who regards the palladium theme as already honoured, and I cannot make that disappear by argument. Kosugi's priority is a real historical fact that the citation wording only partly resolves. The method is also conceptually narrower than degradation, since it concerns one bond type, and I accept that a prize built on a design principle would be the more ambitious choice. Finally, I note that I changed nothing in my credited names while the committee has not shown a majority for any configuration; the lack of five votes is a reason to keep reasoning, not a reason to move.

responses.point: Brzezinski accepts that B057 is strong on impact and maturity, but asks whether Buchwald and Hartwig's step beyond Kosugi's 1983 tin-amide coupling is a new reaction or a development, and whether the distance from the 2010 prize needs a concrete argument.
responses.response: I think the answer is that it is a new catalytic reaction in every way that matters for use. Removing tin was not a cosmetic change. It replaced a stoichiometric toxic reagent with free amines and base, which required a different mechanism: amine coordination, deprotonation at palladium and C-N reductive elimination, which the ligand controls. That is why scope went from a handful of substrates to a general method. So I would keep two names and let the citation say general catalytic coupling. If the expert record shows that Kosugi already demonstrated catalytic turnover with free amines, I would reconsider a third name, but I know of no evidence for that. I am glad this is your first alternative.

responses.point: Aili holds that degradation introduces a new design principle and modality, that C-N coupling extends a tool class honoured in 2010, and that the lack of an approved PROTAC weighs less than the structurally validated concept.
responses.response: I take the design-principle argument seriously, and B004 is my first alternative for that reason. Two things keep me from moving. First, the credit problem is not solved: you and Chabes both name Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, but my own opening placed Handa third because the cereblon strand is the one with a marketed-drug history through thalidomide analogues, and a three-person cap cannot cover both strands. If you want a citation on induced proximity to the ubiquitin system, the committee has to say who is excluded and why. Second, a prize is judged by consequences already shown, and for degraders those are largely clinical-stage promises. C-N coupling is not an extension of 2010 in the sense you mean, since it needed new ligands and addressed a different elementary step.

responses.point: Linke proposes a two-part prize pairing B057 with base editing credited to Liu alone, as two different kinds of chemistry that each fit in one sentence.
responses.response: I agree that B057 is the strongest part and the pairing keeps the union at three names. But I do not support adding B058 this year. A Liu-only citation leaves out Komor and Gaudelli, who carried out the decisive experiments, and the independent Nishida and Kondo cytidine deaminase work, and I would not want the committee to make that cut for the sake of fitting a second part. The chemical step, deamination, is known; the new contribution is protein engineering and directed evolution, and the 2020 genome-editing prize is a close predecessor. I ranked it fifth and nothing in round 1 moved it. If the committee insists on two parts, I would sooner see B004 than B058, though I still prefer a single clean part.

responses.point: Zou prefers to keep Buchwald and Hartwig alone and not add Kosugi or a third name, and asks Somfai whether the priority question could move two names to three.
responses.response: We agree on two names. On your question about Kosugi, I would add a point from the simulation side: the mechanistic picture that made the reaction predictable was developed after the catalytic systems appeared, which is a sign that the generality came from the ligand work and not from the 1983 observation. I would add that being overdue is not itself an argument, as you say, and my support rests on demonstrated consequences. I also agree that the sequencing credit (B012) is harder to resolve than the C-N case, which is why it is my second alternative and not my preference.

responses.point: Somfai argues that the distinction from 2010 is chemical, that Kosugi's stannylamine chemistry used stoichiometric tin with narrow scope, and that a two-name configuration is cleaner than adding a name to soften the priority point.
responses.response: I agree, and your point about different bottlenecks is the one I would put in front of colleagues who see C-N coupling as an extension of 2010. As the person closest to the synthetic literature, you are better placed than I am to check the detailed priority record, and I hope the committee relies on that. I would also keep your question about a two-part prize separate from the credit question: I do not think a second part strengthens the case, since the part added would be weaker than B057 on maturity or attribution.

uncertainties: Whether a majority regards C-N coupling as distinct enough from the 2010 prize; I cannot settle this by argument alone.
Whether the expert record shows catalytic turnover with free amines before the ligand-enabled systems, which would be the one finding that could move me to three names.
Whether degraders (B004) will be treated as one induced-proximity discovery or two, and whether Ciulli or Handa holds the third place; this affects my alternative but not my preference.
I rely on recalled, not newly verified, details of the 1983 to mid-1990s priority record and on current clinical status for degraders.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate. My connections are to Arieh Warshel (EVB collaboration) and the Uppsala structural biology and ribosome community, none of whom are credited on the shortlist. I have served on the committee with Peter Brzezinski since 2015, and this does not touch B057 or my alternatives. No change since round 1.
